Master's Paper

children.name: Approved paper proposal, and the master's paper reviewed by the advisor and a reader

rules.desc:
Submit an approved laboratory research or library-based paper proposal by the last day of instruction in the first quarter of the master's degree program.
Both tracks are required to enroll in ANTHRO 441 Master’s Project in the final quarter of the MA degree program and earn a grade of B or better.
By Week 6 of Graduating Quarter, submit the Master's paper reviewed by two faculty members (advisor and reader).

• For the Culture and Society track, the paper can be a field research or library-based research paper.

• For the Archaeology track, the paper can also be a laboratory research paper.
Optional: Presentation of the master’s research project at the department’s Master’s (Honors) paper presentation event in spring quarter

rules.name: Recommended Course
rules.desc: Students are encouraged to enroll in ANTHRO 299 for Winter and Spring quarters.

gpa: A minimum overall grade of 'B' is needed for the MA coursework.
grading:
A program of 45 units, taken at the 100 level or higher with a minimum grade of 'B'. Of the 45 units:

• At least 23 of the 45 units must be taken at the 200/300 level.

• No more than 5 units may be taken for a satisfactory/no credit grade.

• No more than 10 units of directed reading-style course work may be counted towards the degree.
policies:
Requirements for the coterminal and terminal master’s degree program include the following:

• A faculty advisor appointed in the Department of Anthropology.

• Reach out to your advisor by the first week of Autumn quarter to schedule an initial meeting regarding your degree plan

• Submit the Plan of Study Form found on the department website.

• A self-designed plan of study chosen from one of the following Anthropology tracks; the tracks are not declarable in Axess:

• Archaeology

• Culture and Society
Enrollment for Terminal MA
Graduate enrollment at Stanford University for three consecutive quarters of full tuition for at least 45 units is required of all candidates for the terminal master’s degree. The MA program may require more than one year of study.
Note: completion of the approved course of study for the M.A. should be confirmed before submitting a Request for Terminal Graduate Registration to the Doctoral Degree Program via the Ph.D. or other Professional degree Home Department or Program.
transferPolicy:
No more than 15 units may be approved from related areas of study or overseas studies. See more details on procedure for requesting on the website.
The university allows no transfer units into the master’s program. To provide a meaningful master’s program within one year, advance planning of coursework with a faculty advisor is required.
reviewNotes: Your track decides the track courses and the theory and methods courses, which need a B+ or better. The audit also checks ANTHRO 310G for three quarters, four 5-unit ANTHRO electives numbered 200 or above, and ANTHRO 441 with a B or better. Your graduate units must reach 45 with a B or better in each course: none below the 100 level, at least 23 units at the 200 or 300 level, at most 5 units S/NC, at most 10 units of directed reading, and at least 30 units in ANTHRO, since at most 15 may come from related areas or overseas study. You check by hand the paper proposal and master's paper, the B average, your advisor and Plan of Study Form, and for the terminal MA three quarters of full-tuition enrollment. ANTHRO 299 is only recommended.
